newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shrs rally to new 33-month high by close.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shrs rally to new 33-month high by close.

text.p: ** (1005 GMT) Foreign fund buying and local speculative
support drive Bombay shares to new 33-month high
** Benchmark Bombay index ends 96.41 points, or 2.24
Heavy foreign fund buying powered Bombay shares to new 33-month peaks on Wednesday and brokers said they expect the market to continue the bull run.
"There's been frenzied buying by FIIs (foreign institutional investors)," said Sanat Dalal, a top broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). "They are accumulating all the blue-chips."
The 30-share BSE index finished 96.41 points, or 2.24 percent, higher at a provisional 4,402.80 -- breaking through 4,400 for the first time since mid October 1994.
"It has crossed the barrier. The market looks in very good shape," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 36.10 points, or 3.0 percent, to a provisional 1,238.90.
Buyers on the NSE were encouraged by the start of new weekly account, brokers said.
Traders said the buoyant market was drawing more investors in while sellers were becoming more choosy.
"The biggest point to note is that the most prominent seller has stopped selling," said Dalal, referring to the Unit Trust of India, the country's largest mutual fund.
Other dealers said foreign funds were enlarging their portfolio by buying into new sectors.
"The FIIs are strengthening their portfolio by adding multinational shares to other blue-chips," Arun Shah, chief dealer at brokerage P.R. Subramanyan & Sons.
Traders said MTNL, Castrol, Colgate, TISCO, TELCO, Nestle, HDFC, Reliance and Dr. Reddy's were some of the shares bought by FIIs.
